YES

The script verifies identical key sets across all three checkpoints and bit-exact equality of every non-MLP tensor before any merge, computes each of the 64 MLP tensors in float32 against the unmodified base with lambda 0.4 and casts back to the base dtype, copies all other tensors from the base unchanged, asserts exactly 64 merged and 244 output tensors, and writes a single `out/T4/model.safetensors`. The duplicate `import json` and the optional output-directory argument are harmless and do not affect the default invocation.
